sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed the petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. for the damages caused to its Bus.
02.

The facts in brief of the petitioner's case is that, on 15.11.2019 at about 4.30 p.m. when the driver of the petitioner corporation was driving his BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-53-F-174 slowly and carefully by following traffic rules and regulations in the schedule on route No.258C/15 near Makali Bus stand, Tumakur-Bengaluru NH-48 Service road, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru dist.

at that time, one Tata vehicle bearing Regn.No. KA-01-8587 which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the front right side driver door of the bus.
Due to the accident, petitioner's bus has got damaged.
The petitioner has incurred expenses of Rs.50,000/- including labour and material charges and sustained loss due to damages to the bus and could not fly on road.
The accident was taken place only due to sole rash and negligent driving of the Tata vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01- 8587 belonged to the 1st respondent and the same is insured with 2nd respondent.
Hence, both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the damages to the petitioner.
03. Respondent No.1 remained absent inspite of service of summons, hence he was placed exparte.

Though the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel, has not filed written statement.
04. Based on the above pleadings my predecessor in office has framed following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, on 15.11.2019 at about 4.30 p.m. when the driver of the petitioner corporation bearing Reg. No.KA- Bangalore Metropolitan Transport ... vs Johnpal B on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113277696/
2 53-F-174 was proceeding in his schedule route i.e. No.258C/15 trip and when he reached near Makali Bus stand, Tumakur-Bengaluru NH-48 Service road, at that time, one Tata/LPT/709/38EX vehicle bearing Regn.No. KA-01-8587 drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the front right side driver door of the BMTC bus and due to which the bus got damaged?
2. Whether the petitioner further proves that he had spent more than Rs.11,930/- towards spare parts and repair charges and a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards damages and other expenses?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from whom and how much?
4. What order or Award?
05. In order to prove the case, petitioner got examined the driver as PW.1 and its Depot Manager in Depot No.40 as P.W-2 and produced 19 documents, which were marked as Ex.P1 to 19.
The respondent neither lead evidence nor produced documents.
06. Heard arguments on both the sides.

09. The Petitioner in order to prove the damages caused to the bus due to the accident occurred on 15.11.2019 has examined its driver as PW1 by filing affidavit as his examination in-chief and produced 19 documents.
The averments made in the affidavit filed by him is in consonance with the petition averments.
The petitioner deposed that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata vehicle bearing No.KA-01-8587 driven by its driver.

In order to substantiate his oral evidence, petitioner has produced vehicle location extract, day-to-day report, driving licence, FIR, FIS, charge sheet, vehicle mahazar, sketch, 2 IMV reports at Ex.P2 to 3,
5 to 13.
10.

Firstly, in connection with the ownership of the vehicle bearing registration No.KA-53-F-174 is concerned, in the evidence of PW1-Janardana and PW2-Chandrakala, stated that the petitioner BMTC is the owner of the vehicle in question.
PW.1 is working as driver with the said vehicle and PW2 is working as Depo Manager of Depo No.40.

On 15.11.2019., when he was on duty of the BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-53-F-174 met with an accident, due to the rash and negligent driving Bangalore Metropolitan Transport ... vs Johnpal B on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113277696/
3 of the Tata/LPT/709/38EX vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-8587.

sentences.text: Consequently, bus was damaged.
In support of the said affidavit evidence, the PW1 on behalf of the petitioner placed Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 for consideration.

The said documents are police documents and Job card and also letter dated 20.08.2020.
11.

On going through the said documents, it reflect that, on the basis of first information given by PW-1, on the same day of the accident criminal law was set in motion against the driver of Tata/LPT/709/38EX vehicle bearing registration No. KA-01-8587 alleging that, he had committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC.
After due investigation process, final report has been submitted against the driver of the said vehicle by name Devarajegowda M.J.
The said document and also the recitals of spot mahazar, spot sketch and complaint, it is crystal clear that, in the accident in question, vehicle belonged to the petitioner was damaged.

The said vehicle was defending vehicle in the said accident and also driver of the Tata/LPT/709/38EX vehicle bearing registration No. KA-01-8587.
12.

Secondly, it is the assertion of the petitioner through the evidence of PW2 that, due to the accident, front shape right side damaged, right side front portion body damaged/dented, front right side mirror unit damaged and front windscreen glass damage.
Due to the said damages, bus in question was unable to complete the schedule trip on the said day and the corporation was suffered monetary loss.

13. In support of the said stand of the PW-1 and PW.2 were placed his authorization letter, vehicle location report, day-to-day activity report, driving licence, ticket, first information report, accident report, charge sheet, spot mahazar, vehicle seizure mahazar, sketch, IMV reports, job card, In and out register, trip sheet, R.C. marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19 for consideration.

In the recitals of the Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.16, there is a clear narration about the vehicle number and name of the driver deputed as on the date of the accident and the route also been noted in the said documents.
As per the Ex.P.12 & 13, the bus was damaged to its front shape right side, right side front portion body dented, front right side mirror unit and front windscreen glass.
But there is no document to show the actual loss, no other supportive documentary evidence is available on record.

14. Over all appreciation of the evidence of the PW-1 and PW.2 along with the documentary evidence, there is no dispute that, due to the accident, vehicle of the petitioner corporation was damaged and also there is no dispute with respect to the ownership of the vehicle in question.
Further, on going through the Ex.P.4 driving licence, it is evident that, at the time of accident, the driver of the vehicle belonged to the petitioner had valid and effective driving license.

At the time of cross-examination of PW-1, he stated that, he being the driver of the bus belonged to the petitioner,
as on the date of accident, was proceeding in the schedule route, at that time offending vehicle came and caused the accident and he gave complaint to the police.
In this regard, both the vehicles were seized and the vehicle pertaining to the petitioner was taken to the interim custody, after the accident.
And denied the suggestion of other side that, due to his sole negligence, accident in question had taken place and false complaint has been given against the driver of the offending vehicle.
But, no important points culled out from the mouth of this witness to show that, the vehicle of the petitioner was not damaged in the accident.

Hence, I am of the view that, in support of the above issue, the petitioner corporation has placed satisfactory evidence for consideration.

16. It is relevant to note that, for compensation filed U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident, only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required, as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in, 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text:
Further, It was observed that, "When the accident, from the driver of the offending vehicle is proved,
clearly indicates that, due to the said mistake on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the defending vehicle was damaged."

17. In the light of my due discussions held above, I am of the view that, the evidence of the PW1 and PW2 and also the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner substantiates the case of the petitioner.

Hence, I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved its case that, the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle Tata/LPT/709/38EX vehicle bearing registration No. KA-01-8587.
In the said accident, the defending vehicle BMTC bus, bearing registration No.KA-53-F- 174, belonged to the petitioner was damaged.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2 :

The petitioner being the owner of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-53-F-174 has contended that, after the accident, vehicle in question belonged to the petitioner sustained damages to its back side, due to which petitioner has suffered a loss of Rs.50,000/- .
In order to prove the same, PW.1 has produced job card, letter dt.20.08.2020.

Petitioner has also examined PW2 who is the Depot Manager in respondent Corporation in depot No.40 has produced vehicle in and out registers, Inventory register and RC which were marked as Ex.P16 to Ex.P19 which are corroborating with the damages mentioned in the F.I.S, and damages mentioned in IMV report marked as Ex.P12 & 13.
Ex. P12
& 13 reveals that the bus has sustained damages of front shape right side, right side front portion body dented, front wind screen glass broken.
Hence there is corroboration on comparison of First Information and IMV report.
In the evidence PW.2 deposed that the bus has sustained damages to its mirror unit and front right side of the body of the bus and it is been repaired.
The repair has been done in their garage itself and the bus was there in the garage for a period of 10 days.
In this regard, the petitioner corporation has produced job card at Ex.P14 which reflects that the petitioner has incurred Rs.11,930/- for repairing the bus.

It is further contended that due to the accident bus unable to complete the trip on the said day further 267km cancelled and it has incurred loss of Rs.11,930/-.
19.

Along with the evidence of PW-1 and PW2, on going through the material documents, reveal that, in the trip sheets there is a clear mention about plying of the defending vehicle in question, as on the date of the accident.

But, there is no supportive documentary evidence is available on record,
in proof of the how much amount has been lost by the petitioner.

sentences.text: On the other hand, Ex.P.16 and 17, discloses about in and out registers and work charts.
These documents will not support the stand of the PW1 and PW2 to the effect that, due to the damages of the bus the petitioner corporation incurred a monetary loss.

21. At the time of cross-examination of PW-1, answers given by the PW1 reveals that, on the same date of sending the vehicle for repair, the bus in question was out from the workshop, in case of accident to route bus, they send the spier bus to the said route as altarnate to the accidental vehicle and admitted that, the corporation has not placed any documents to show the monetary loss bills for having paid the expenses of the purchasing of spare parts of the bus and also not produced trip cancelled document.

22. Over all appreciation of the documents and the evidence given by the PW1 and PW2, I am of the view that, the petitioner corporation has not placed satisfactory and convincing documents to show that, a sum of Rs.30,000/- loss of was caused to the corporation.

Hence, by considering the documents, placed by the petitioner corporation, along with the damages noted in the report of the motor vehicle inspector marked at Ex.P.14, I am of the view that, it is apt to award compensation of Rs.11,930/- towards damages of the vehicle.
The same will meet the ends of justice.

23. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, keeping in mind about the damages mentioned in the recitals of the IMV report, and also inconvenience caused to the petitioner, due to the said damage, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,930/-
(Rupees Eleven thousand nine hundred and thirty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
24. In the present case the 1st respondent though appeared through his counsel, but has not filed written statement nor contested the case.
Hence, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-8587 shall indemnify the respondent No.1 in paper of compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the above the respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answered this issue partly in the affirmative.

25. Issue No.3:- In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,930/-(Rupees Eleven thousand nine hundred and thirty only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
